chunks: Concerning a man who delays al-ẓuhr until the time of al-ʿaṣr enters: he begins with al-ʿaṣr, then he performs al-ẓuhr.
The correct understanding of this report is that when the time of al-ʿaṣr becomes constrained, he begins with it, then after it he performs al-ẓuhr, according to what we explained in detail earlier.
Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAbbās, from Ismāʿīl ibn Hammām, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, that he said:

key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.تَضَيَّقَ وَقْتُ الْعَصْرِ: the time of al-ʿaṣr has become constrained or limited
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْعَصْرِ: the time assigned for the afternoon salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَبْدَأُ بِالْعَصْرِ: he begins by performing al-ʿaṣr first

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone delays al-ẓuhr until the time of al-ʿaṣr becomes tight?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling on one who delays al-ẓuhr until the time of al-ʿaṣr has entered. It clarifies that if the time for al-ʿaṣr has become tight, al-ʿaṣr is to be performed first, then al-ẓuhr afterward, reflecting a jurisprudential ordering based on the constriction of prayer time.
